item.title: Latest on USS Lincoln as it heads home to San Diego
item.description: The USS Abraham Lincoln has left the Middle East and is cruising back to its home port of San Diego after a record-long deployment. CBS News' Charlie D'Agata has more.

item.title: Pentagon moves to fire publisher and editor of Stars and Stripes
item.description: The Pentagon has given separation notices to both the publisher and the editor-in-chief of Stars and Stripes, according to people familiar with the matter.

item.title: Trump campaigning for Darline Graham after debate gaffe
item.description: President Trump is in South Carolina Friday night to campaign for Sen. Darline Graham as she continues her campaign for a full term in her late brother Lindsey Graham's Senate seat. CBS News' Nikole Killion reports.

item.title: Body of New York grandmother who went missing in Las Vegas found, sister says
item.description: The body of Alisa Goods, a New York grandmother who went missing while visiting Las Vegas, has been found after more than a week, her sister told CBS News' Alice Gainer.

item.title: What to know as Lindsay Clancy trial nears closing arguments
item.description: The defense rested Friday in Lindsay Clancy's murder trial for the killings of her three young children. CBS News' Shanelle Kaul reports on the case.

item.title: "Everything as it was": Explore the bedrooms of kids killed in school shootings
item.description: The families of nine school shooting victims opened their doors to Steve Hartman and photographer Lou Bopp, allowing them to document their children's bedrooms.

item.title: Trump says Iran "not ready to make the right deal" as U.S. turns to economic warfare
item.description: As Vice President JD Vance declares economic pressure "the most effective tool that we have," Iran seeks to show deepening trade ties with its neighbors.

item.title: Psychiatrist testifies that Lindsay Clancy told children "go to God"
item.description: The defense rested in Lindsay Clancy's murder trial Friday in Massachusetts. The prosecution has started calling rebuttal witnesses.

item.title: Supreme Court lets Trump's White House ballroom project continue for now
item.description: The Supreme Court on Friday temporarily allowed President Trump's White House ballroom construction to continue. CBS News chief legal correspondent Jan Crawford has the details.

item.title: USS Lincoln leaves Middle East after 9-month deployment as Trump ramps up economic pressure on Iran
item.description: The USS Washington arrived in the Middle East from Asia on Thursday and relieved the USS Lincoln after a nine-month deployment. The move comes as the Trump administration says it will unveil the "toughest sanctions" on Iran. CBS News' Margaret Brennan and Elliot Ackerman have more.

item.title: Man who took final photo of Tupac testifies about lead-up to murder
item.description: The man who took the last known photo of Tupac Shakur testified on Friday in the trial of a man accused of organizing the rapper's killing. CBS News legal reporter Katrina Kaufman has the latest.

item.title: Sword attack at school in Sweden leaves 1 dead, police say
item.description: An 18-year-old with a sword attacked a school Friday in central Sweden, killing one person and seriously injuring at least two others.

item.title: Watch: Severe storms slam the Northeast
item.description: Heavy rain and winds battered parts of the Northeast United States on Thursday, with some states even reporting tornadoes. These videos show the conditions on the ground as storms moved over the area. Then, CBS News' Jared Ochacher and Jessica Burch join with a look at the damage and the latest forecast.

item.title: This week on "Sunday Morning" (Aug. 23)
item.description: A look at the features for this week's broadcast of the Emmy-winning program, hosted by Jane Pauley.

item.title: Book excerpt: "The Serviceberry" by Robin Wall Kimmerer
item.description: The #1 New York Times bestselling author of "Braiding Sweetgrass" writes about embracing gratitude and reciprocity in our dealings with nature, and the importance of recognizing and sharing the many gifts the world gives us.

item.title: TikTok agrees to pay $400 million to settle child privacy lawsuit
item.description: The Justice Department sued TikTok in 2024, alleging that it violated a U.S. law prohibiting the collection of kids' data.

item.title: 8 dead in charter plane crash near remote military radar site in Alaska
item.description: The crash of a small plane in Alaska chartered by the U.S. Army Corps of Engineers is under investigation.

item.title: Walmart to let shoppers use Apple Pay and other tap-to-pay methods
item.description: Walmart will let shoppers use tap-to-pay methods, including Apple Pay and Google Pay, beginning later this month.

item.title: Supreme Court temporarily allows work on White House ballroom to continue
item.description: Chief Justice John Roberts issued a stay that will remain in place until the Supreme Court takes further action.

item.title: Nearly 25% of workers are "functionally unemployed," analysis finds
item.description: An alternative measure of unemployment that accounts for wages suggests the U.S. labor market is weaker than it looks.

item.title: Russian strike kills 15 people at shopping mall in Zelenskyy's hometown
item.description: Zelenskyy described the attack as a double-tap strike, in which an initial wave of drones hit the area, followed by a second wave as rescue workers responded.

item.title: Controversial pro-Trump attorney Ed Martin leaving administration
item.description: Ed Martin, the pro-Trump lawyer who has been at the center of several controversies, is departing the administration, the president announced.

item.title: People are scrambling to find wads of cash dropped all over American cities
item.description: Cash drop social media accounts have people racing to find money hidden across the country. Here's what's behind the viral videos.

item.title: Wads of cash are being hidden across the U.S. Here's the backstory.
item.description: Across the U.S., hidden cash drops like these have sent people running to find the money — and given many people hope of a windfall. CBS News' Graham Kates gives us a look at the social media accounts that promote them.

item.title: "Face the Nation with Margaret Brennan" guests for Aug. 23, 2026
item.description: This week's guests include Democratic Rep. Seth Moulton of Massachusetts and Republican Rep. Byron Donalds of Florida.

item.title: Drug mix-up at hospital causes dire complications in 4 patients
item.description: Four patients at Ascension Saint Thomas Midtown received incorrect medications last week, CBS affiliate WTVF reported.

item.title: AI companies accused of hoarding and destroying millions of books
item.description: Consumer advocates are urging the FTC to examine whether AI developers are hurting competition and reducing public access to source material.

item.title: Notable Deaths in 2026
item.description: A look back at the esteemed personalities who've left us this year, who'd touched us with their innovation, creativity and humanity.

item.title: USS Abraham Lincoln leaving Middle East after 9-month deployment
item.description: The aircraft carrier and its 5,000 crew members will return to San Diego after an approximately nine-month deployment.

item.title: Trump directs CDC to align with assessment calling for fewer childhood vaccines
item.description: Earlier this year, the CDC announced updated recommendations that would reduce the number of recommended immunizations for children from 17 to 11.
